title: The Garou
summary: Werewolves: wolf, human and spirit in one body, sworn to defend Gaia.

claims.text: A werewolf is a blend of wolf, human and spirit.
The Garou were set to be the protectors of the world, while other shapeshifters got other tasks.
The First Change is a terrible shock, and comes later in life for homid Garou than for lupus.

title: The Impergium
summary: An ancient age when werewolves culled humanity and taught it to fear the wild.

claims.text: In the Impergium humans came to dread the wilderness, and wolves above all; the fear lingers today.
Humans banded into settlements for safety at night, and those grew into farming villages.
The Red Talons hold that ending the Impergium was the one mistake.

title: The War of Rage
summary: The ancient war in which the Garou turned on the other shapeshifters.

claims.text: Gaia gave the shapeshifting gift to many animals, each with its own task.
Few Fera still trust the Garou, and shapeshifters remember the War of Rage for a very long time.

title: The Delirium
summary: The madness and lost memory that strike humans who see a werewolf in war form.

claims.text: Humans who look on a Garou in Crinos form suffer madness and memory loss.
Some part of the human collective unconscious remembers thousands of years of being preyed on by werewolves.
Kinfolk are not prone to the Delirium.

title: The Litany
summary: The code of law every Garou must keep, whatever tribe.

claims.text: Traditions differ by tribe, but all Garou are held to the Litany.
The full Litany reads like a long poem as well as a body of law, and reciting it whole takes hours.
No Garou disputes the tenet against violating a caern, since losing one to ruin or taint kills part of the Earth.

title: Caerns
summary: Sacred places where the Garou reach the spirit world.

claims.text: A caern is a sacred meeting place for contact with the spirit world.
The Gauntlet is weakest around caerns.
Moots meet at caerns, and a Moon Bridge links one caern to another.

title: Septs and Moots
summary: The Garou who hold and guard a caern, and their gatherings.

claims.text: Moots are gatherings of a sept or a tribe, held at a caern.
The bawn is the guarded border land that rings a caern.

title: Packs
summary: A small band of Garou bound by friendship and a shared task.

claims.text: Packs run from two to ten werewolves, ideally with each auspice present.
Garou from rival tribes can grow closer than blood kin after running together long enough.
A totem spirit is the binding force that holds a pack together, and the pack chooses the totem that suits it.

title: Breeds
summary: A werewolf's breed comes from the mother's natural form.

claims.text: Each Garou's breed follows the natural form of the mother.
Homids may buy any Ability during character creation.
Homids start with 1 Gnosis; metis start with 3.
Metis are the sterile offspring of two Garou, usually scorned, and each has at least one deformity chosen at creation.
Abstract thought comes newer to lupus than to homids.

title: Metis
summary: The child of two werewolves, born deformed into the bottom of Garou society.

claims.text: Metis come from two Garou parents, a union that breaks the Litany.
Every metis has at least one deformity, chosen at character creation.
Mule is slang for metis.

title: Auspices
summary: The moon phase at birth, which shapes a werewolf's role.

claims.text: The auspice is the phase of the moon at a Garou's birth, thought to set personality and leanings.
Ragabash, the New Moon trickster, starts with 1 Rage.
Theurge, the Crescent Moon seer and mystic, starts with 2 Rage.
Philodox, the Half Moon judge, starts with 3 Rage.
Galliard, the passionate counterpart to the stoic Philodox, starts with 4 Rage.
Ahroun, the Full Moon warrior, starts with 5 Rage.

title: Black Furies
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Black Furies are daughters of Luna as Artemis, tracing their origins to Greece and Asia Minor as defenders of the Wyld.
A Black Furies character starts with 3 Willpower.
Their totem is Pegasus.

title: Bone Gnawers
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Bone Gnawers, Children of Rat, hunt territory and breed with Kin that no other tribe wants.
A Bone Gnawers character starts with 4 Willpower.

title: Children of Gaia
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Children of Gaia are Gaia's warriors who want peace above all, and work hardest for cooperation between the tribes.
A Children of Gaia character starts with 4 Willpower.

title: Fianna
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Fianna, Tribe of Stag, delight in the pleasures of the flesh, song and battle.
A Fianna character starts with 3 Willpower.
They have no Background restrictions.

title: Get of Fenris
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Get of Fenris, or Fenrir, are the most warlike tribe and prize a glorious death over peaceful old age.
A Get of Fenris character starts with 3 Willpower.

title: Glass Walkers
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Glass Walkers blend technology and shamanism, prefer the city to the wild, and defend urban places.
A Glass Walkers character starts with 3 Willpower.

title: Red Talons
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Red Talons hold that humanity is a pestilence and the Impergium should never have ended.
A Red Talons character starts with 3 Willpower.

title: Shadow Lords
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Shadow Lords keep a rigid internal hierarchy, and other tribes distrust their manipulative ways.
A Shadow Lords character starts with 3 Willpower.

title: Silent Striders
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Silent Striders wander between caerns, carrying news and scouting for the Garou Nation.
A Silent Striders character starts with 3 Willpower.

title: Silver Fangs
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Silver Fangs, tribe of Falcon, claim to lead the Garou Nation by a bloodline traced to the Progenitor Wolf.
A Silver Fangs character starts with 3 Willpower.

title: Stargazers
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Stargazers are the smallest tribe, following meditation, philosophy and lucid dreaming to master the self.
A Stargazers character starts with 4 Willpower.

title: Uktena
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Uktena were the wise Older Brother of the three Pure Ones and gathered mystical lore, settling across the Americas.
A Uktena character starts with 3 Willpower.

title: Wendigo
summary: A tribe of the Garou Nation, one of thirteen.

claims.text: The Wendigo have long memories of the Europeans who came to the Americas and the tribes who came with them.
A Wendigo character starts with 4 Willpower.

title: The Thirteen Tribes
summary: The tribes of the Garou Nation, the largest social unit among werewolves.

claims.text: A tribe is the largest social unit of Garou, often bound by bloodline, similar totems and ways of life.
Each tribe sets a starting Willpower and a list of beginning Gifts.

title: The Lost Tribes
summary: Three tribes the Garou Nation no longer counts: the Bunyip, the Croatan and the White Howlers.

claims.text: The Bunyip guarded Australia, a land with no wolves, and some doubted they were werewolves at all.
The Croatan, Middle Brother of the Pure Ones, gave their lives to banish a great evil.
The White Howlers were feared warriors whose corruption made them the Black Spiral Dancers.

title: Black Spiral Dancers
summary: The one werewolf tribe wholly given over to the Wyrm.

claims.text: The Black Spiral Dancers alone among werewolf tribes have turned entirely to the Wyrm.
A petitioner must betray former allies, forsake former beliefs and descend into madness.
They carry a wide range of mental disorders.
The Tribe Novel Black Spiral Dancers and Wendigo tells that a Hive wastes none of its fallen: even the mortally wounded may be buried alive in the breeding pits to serve it further.

title: Fomori
summary: Humans corrupted by the Wyrm in mind, body and spirit.

claims.text: A fomor is usually made by a Bane possessing the whole body.
Each fomor gets supernatural power from the Wyrm and is always marked or deformed in some way.

title: Pentex
summary: A multinational holding company, Wyrm-tainted, behind a web of corrupt firms.

claims.text: Pentex has lasted for decades and spreads its taint through a vast number of subsidiaries.

title: The Triat
summary: Three cosmic forces: Wyld, Weaver and Wyrm.

claims.text: The Triat is the trinity of primal cosmic forces: Weaver, Wyld and Wyrm.
The Garou hold that the three shape and rule eternity while working against each other.

title: The Wyrm
summary: The corrupting force of the Triat that the Garou war against.

claims.text: Banes are evil spirits that follow the Wyrm.
The Apocalypse is the time of the last battle with the Wyrm, and many believe it is now.
Rage is Gaia's anger at the plunder of the world by the Weaver and the Wyrm.

title: Banes
summary: Evil spirits in the Wyrm's service.

claims.text: There are many kinds of Banes, Scrags and Kali among them.

title: Gaia
summary: The Mother of the Garou, the living world.

claims.text: Gaia's form is ultimately unknowable, yet it surrounds the Garou as the living essence of creation.
Celestines are the greatest spirits, the nearest the Garou have to gods, such as Luna and Helios.

title: The Umbra
summary: The spirit world around and beyond the physical world.

claims.text: The Near Umbra is the spirit world around the Gaian Realm; the Deep Umbra lies outside the Membrane and grows more broken the farther one goes.
The Penumbra is the closest part of the Umbra.
Near Umbral Realms circle the Earth, separated from the physical world by a barrier.

title: The Gauntlet
summary: The wall that parts the Umbra from the physical world.

claims.text: The Gauntlet runs thickest where the Weaver's technology rules and thinnest at caerns.
Gnosis is a Garou's link to the spirit world.

title: Rage
summary: Gaia's anger burning in every werewolf.

claims.text: Rage points are spent at the start of a turn, during declaration, and only in times of stress.
Rank raises frenzy difficulties: +1 at Rank 3, +2 at Ranks 4 and 5.

title: Gnosis
summary: The Garou's spiritual link to Gaia and the spirit world.

claims.text: Gnosis is Gaia's other gift to the Garou, linking them to the spirit world.
Like Rage and Willpower, Gnosis has a permanent rating and a pool of points.

title: Renown
summary: How well a werewolf lives up to the role expected in Garou society.

claims.text: Renown measures how well a character fills the expected role, and so is closely tied to auspice.
Unlike experience, Renown reflects standing among the Garou.

title: Rank
summary: The strict ladder of status among the Garou.

claims.text: Among the Garou, rank sets status and how much respect a character is owed.

title: The Five Forms
summary: Homid, Glabro, Crinos, Hispo and Lupus.

claims.text: Each step between forms takes one success, so human to wolf takes four.
Shifting from Homid is difficulty 6; from Hispo it is difficulty 7.
Spending a Rage point changes form at once with no roll, and any Garou can return to breed form instantly.
Crinos, the war form, adds Strength +4, Dexterity +1 and Stamina +3, and stands eight to ten feet.
Glabro, the near-human, adds Strength +2 and Stamina +2 with Manipulation -2 and Appearance -1.
Hispo, the dire wolf, adds Strength +3, Dexterity +2 and Stamina +3.
Lupus, the wolf, adds Strength +1, Dexterity +2 and Stamina +2.

title: Kinfolk
summary: Humans and wolves related to the Garou who are not werewolves.

claims.text: Kinfolk are human or wolf relatives of the Garou who do not suffer the Delirium.
Kinfolk are not only families but the Garou Nation's support, from guards to bankers.

title: Totems
summary: The spirits that bind packs together.

claims.text: A totem spirit holds a pack together; the pack picks it, though finding it can mean a quest.

title: The Fera
summary: Shapeshifters other than werewolves.

claims.text: Fera is the Garou word for other shapeshifters, most of whom are thought extinct.
Long ago the Fera stood with the Garou as allies.
